newsitem.title: USA: CME live hogs, pork bellies post limit gains.
newsitem.headline: CME live hogs, pork bellies post limit gains.

text.p: CME live hog and pork belly futures posted limit gains in some contracts at mid-morning Friday on continued reaction from Thursday's news that Taiwan will suspend pork exports because of foot-and-mouth disease in that country, traders said.

Traders said Japan and South Korea, which buy Taiwanese pork, will likely turn to the U.S. for some of the expected shortfall left by the Taiwan ban. This perceived demand already has CME traders expecting $1.00 to $2.00 per cwt higher cash hog prices next week.

Forecasts for high cash hog prices next week and higher cash pork prices late Thursday, also was attributed to the Taiwanese news, and prompted active short covering in the CME hogs and pork belly futures Friday, they said.
University of Missouri economist Glenn Grimes said the Taiwan pork export ban could fuel an increase of $4 to $5 per cwt in U.S. cash hog prices the rest of this year.
At 1109 CST, April to August CME lean hog futures were up the 2.00 cent limit with April at 72.275 cents per lb. Pork bellies were up the 3.00-cent limit in May at 78.95 to up 2.175 in August.
